violation_type.title: Naptime Child/Caregiver Ratio - Groups Not Combined Not Reduced (26 TAC §746.1613(a)(2))
violation_type.short_title: Naptime Child/Caregiver Ratio - Groups Not Combined Not Reduced
violation_type.typical_finding: A group of seven children, with one caregiver with the specified age of 12-18 months were not asleep sitting in high chairs and then moved to classroom. This group of children were over ratio.

finding_variants.text: A group of seven children, with one caregiver with the specified age of 12-18 months were not asleep sitting in high chairs and then moved to classroom. This group of children were over ratio.

Inspector observed one caregiver supervising two classrooms during nap time with no additional staff. Two children ages 3-4 yrs. old were in one classroom and the caregiver was in a secondary classroom with infants who were between the ages of 3-14 months old.

There was one caregiver in a room with a specified age group of 12-17 months with 6 children during naptime. Ratios for infants can never be reduced and the correct ratio for the specified age group is 1 caregiver to 5 children. This was corrected at inspection when a second caregiver was asked to come into the room.
The area used in central nap time location were observed with limit space between mats, furniture, and children mats were place in areas that might limited the view of all children.
Inspector observed one staff with 7 infants between the ages of 3-17 months old. There was no extra staff observed at the facility during nap time when the inspector arrived.

The naptime child/caregiver ratio was not met as two divided classrooms were being supervised by one caregiver.  The caregiver was sitting in the middle of two classrooms.  One classroom had 11- 4-year-old children napping.  The other classroom had 10 children napping with a specified age group (SAG) of 3 years old children napping; 7 of which were 3 years old.
